author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Khosla Ventures plans to open its first office outside Silicon Valley this fall, establishing a New York outpost on 14th Street. Investor Keith Rabois confirmed the move at a TechCrunch event, describing it as a significant expansion for a firm that has operated from Menlo Park and does not maintain a San Francisco office.

The new location is expected to house a small group of investors, including Rabois. It will also include an executive briefing center designed to bring groups of portfolio companies together with large corporate customers. The format is intended to help startups pursue pilot projects and commercial relationships rather than functioning only as a traditional deal office.

The expansion adds another major venture-capital name to New York’s startup ecosystem, where firms including Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz already have partners. Khosla’s plan is not a fundraise or a stock event, but it is a concrete capital-market signal: a prominent West Coast investor sees enough portfolio and customer activity to support a permanent East Coast base.
dek: The venture firm expects to open a small New York outpost this fall with an executive briefing center for portfolio companies.
headline: Khosla Ventures plans first office outside Sand Hill Road
